To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NuA 4 HAT E 1 1 differentially affects the transcription of certain groups of genes whereas the SAG A HAT G cn 5 has a weaker and more uniform effect.
the histone acetylase complexes NuA4 and Gcn5 have distinct effects on the expression of different sets of genes, and that the Mediator complex is particularly important at highly transcribed genes.
NuA4, SAGA, and Mediator are deployed in different combinations at different groups of genes to generate moderate or highly expressed transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of histone acetylation and coactivator complexes in transcriptional control.
the role of histone acetylation in gene expression, and we have identified two distinct groups of co-regulated genes, which are regulated by the histone acetyl transferases Esa1 and Gcn5 respectively
the mechanisms by which the cell controls gene expression, in particular, how the cell controls transcription of genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transcriptional coactivator Mediator and two distinct histone acetylase complexes, NuA and SAGA have distinct roles in gene activation.
there are three major classes of yeast genes that require different combinations of Mediator and HATs for their transcriptional activation.
the NuA 4 and SAG A HAT complexes and the Mediator coactivator complex have different roles in transcriptional regulation in yeast.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a complex interplay of coactivator complexes at yeast genes, and that the relative deployment of these complexes at specific genes can be used to classify genes into groups that share a common pattern of regulation.
the transcriptional machinery is not a single entity but a complex network of interacting factors.
Mediator, Esa1 and SAGA have overlapping but distinct roles in gene activation and that these roles are not simply a consequence of their shared subunit Tra1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Mediator, NuA4, SAGA, and other coactivator factors have distinct roles in regulating the transcription of different genes.
the deployment of Mediator, SAGA, and NuA4 at different genes is not uniform, but instead reflects distinct patterns of gene regulation.
there are multiple ways to regulate gene expression.
